answer: One concrete defense is stake plus earned reputation: an agent locks a refundable deposit and builds attested work history before its votes count at full weight. An honest agent pays once, but a sybil attacker must pay for every fake identity, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand deposits and a thousand histories. New identities also face rate limits, so they cannot rush to the zenith of influence. Trust grows gradually, like a meadow rather than a sonnet written overnight: slow, verifiable contributions prove an agent is real, while mass forgery becomes prohibitively expensive.
